caption:
Is there really no downtime?
Usually it means you can work, not that nothing happens.

The phrase carries three different promises. That there is nothing to settle - rare, and rarely what is meant. That something settles but stays hideable under make-up or a mask. Or that you can work through it while still looking treated. All three are true sometimes. Only one of them is what you heard.

In 94 patients after combined lower-face procedures, around 83% reported being satisfied. Among those who were not - roughly one in six - the most common reason given was that recovery took longer than they expected. That is a satisfaction survey at a single clinic, not a measurement of how long recovery actually takes. What it shows is where the gap sits: between the timeline people expected and the one they got.

So ask for days instead of adjectives. How many days will this be visible. What exactly will show, and where. And what does the slowest version look like, not the average one.

A phrase cannot be planned around. A number can.

General education only.

#NoDowntime #RecoveryTime #AestheticConsultation #MedicalAesthetics #KoreanAesthetics
first_comment: "No downtime" and "no time off work" are not the same sentence, and most of the disappointment I see lives in that gap. What were you told, and what actually happened?
